How many stores return an MCP tools list?

In the ShopBot Index crawl of 9 November 2026, 8 of 8 stores we could check return a tools list from an MCP endpoint named in the UCP profile (100.0%). In the ShopBot Index crawl of 9 November 2026, 945 of 2,466 stores we could check name an MCP endpoint in a UCP profile (38.3%). Left out of the tools-list share: 11 stores refused the tools request; 924 stores got HTTP 422 and no tools list (the endpoint responded, but the body was not a tools list we accept); 1 store got HTTP 400 and no tools list; 1 store got no HTTP status and no tools list; 1 store was disallowed by robots.txt; 1,521 stores named no MCP endpoint; 387 stores were not checked for signals. A refusal is not "no". Left out of the endpoint share: 388 stores we couldn't check. A published file or profile is a declaration, not proof that agents can buy. ShopBot Index does not test purchases.

No big retailer met this check in this crawl.

How we check

An MCP endpoint counts only when a UCP profile names one. We send that endpoint one read-only JSON-RPC tools/list request and we never call a tool (UCP specification). A tools list counts only on HTTP 200 when at least one tool is named. HTTP 200, 404 or 410 with no tools list is a check that found none. HTTP 401, 403, 429, 451 or 503 is a refusal and is left out of the tools-list share. Any other HTTP status, including 422, means the endpoint responded but we did not get a tools list we accept, so that store is left out of the tools-list share and is counted as naming an endpoint. A store names an endpoint when the tools request was sent and the endpoint answered, refused, or returned no tools list. A robots.txt disallow, or a check we did not reach, is left out of both shares. A store whose profile names no endpoint is left out of the tools-list share and is in the endpoint share as not naming one. A store counts when at least one of its websites meets the rule. This page counts stores. The Beyond UCP table counts websites, so the two numbers can differ. How we check.

Frequently asked questions

How many stores return an MCP tools list?

In the ShopBot Index crawl of 9 November 2026, 8 of 8 stores we could check return a tools list from an MCP endpoint named in the UCP profile (100.0%). In the ShopBot Index crawl of 9 November 2026, 945 of 2,466 stores we could check name an MCP endpoint in a UCP profile (38.3%). Left out of the tools-list share: 11 stores refused the tools request; 924 stores got HTTP 422 and no tools list (the endpoint responded, but the body was not a tools list we accept); 1 store got HTTP 400 and no tools list; 1 store got no HTTP status and no tools list; 1 store was disallowed by robots.txt; 1,521 stores named no MCP endpoint; 387 stores were not checked for signals. A refusal is not "no". Left out of the endpoint share: 388 stores we couldn't check. A published file or profile is a declaration, not proof that agents can buy. ShopBot Index does not test purchases.

Which big retailers returned a tools list?

No big retailer met this check in this crawl.

Which big retailers name an MCP endpoint?

Big retailers first (12): Asprey, Boozt, FAO Schwarz, Flying Tiger Copenhagen, Hamleys, IKEA, Mexx, Pepco, Poundland, Quiksilver, The Body Shop and Zellers.

An MCP endpoint counts only when a UCP profile names one. We send that endpoint one read-only JSON-RPC tools/list request and we never call a tool (UCP specification). HTTP 401, 403, 429, 451 or 503 is a refusal and is left out of the tools-list share. Any other HTTP status, including 422, means the endpoint responded but we did not get a tools list we accept, so that store is left out of the tools-list share and is counted as naming an endpoint. A robots.txt disallow, or a check we did not reach, is left out of both shares.
